To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the uncertainty of soil water content at the initial condition is the main source of the uncertainty in the simulation of the soil water content in a variably saturated soil.
the initial condition uncertainty in the soil water content has a large effect on the uncertainty of the predicted soil water content.
The initial condition uncertainty is the most important factor in the uncertainty of the simulated soil water content, and it has a significant effect on the simulated soil temperature.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the uncertainty of initial conditions in the variably saturated zone and the effect on the uncertainty of the model output.
the development and application of a new method for estimating the initial condition of a soil moisture profile for variably saturated water flow modeling.
the uncertainty of initial conditions in variably saturated groundwater flow models and the effect of different initialization approaches.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the initial condition of a numerical model for variably saturated flow should be as realistic as possible.
the uncertainty in soil water flow model predictions is due to the uncertainty in the initial and boundary conditions, and the model structure.
the uncertainty of the soil water balance is a function of the initial soil water content, the soil type and the soil water content during the growing period.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the uncertainty in the initial condition of soil moisture content is the main source of uncertainty in the simulation of soil moisture and groundwater levels.

, for a wide range of initial conditions and model parameter values, the initial condition has the largest effect on the model output, followed by model parameter values, and finally the initial condition has a larger effect than model parameters.
the uncertainty of initial conditions and initialization approaches in a variably saturated flow model can be quantified and reduced by the proposed method.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the uncertainty in the initial conditions is not negligible.
the use of the initial condition as a control variable in the optimization of the model parameters is a very powerful technique.
the uncertainty of the initial conditions can be a significant source of model uncertainty in the prediction of the soil moisture.
